name: Wedgewood Blue
lede: Wedgewood Blue is named for the blue of Wedgwood pottery, but the swatch listed under that name is a pale periwinkle that is much lighter than the famous ware.

sections.title: Pottery blue, light or dark
sections.body:
One dictionary defines the name as the blue, light or dark, characteristic of Wedgewood pottery, and it spells the maker with the extra e [1]. Because the pottery comes in both shades, the name never fixed on one color [1]. Our library carries a Wedgewood Blue from Ridgway's 1912 plates, in two places: plate 21 (hue 51', tone f) and plate 9 (hue 53, tone f) [2].

The swatch is a very pale violet-blue, within about ten units of [[periwinkle]] and close to [[pale-violet]] and [[powder-blue]] [2]. The more usual spelling has its own entry, [[wedgwood-blue]], with the same swatch [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, a color within six units of this swatch fills at least five per cent of the canvas in 16, from Piero della Francesca's Battista Sforza (1474) to Sonne's cattle and battle scenes of the 1840s and 1870s, where it covers about a third of the picture [3]. Photographs of aged, varnished paintings can only suggest the original color [3].
